question: Bound average additional public Rust CPU dispatch cost against independent native C++ on the five existing matched workloads
analysis: Equal-weight average of paired process-mean differences; Student t bounds across process blocks, with approximate coverage conditional on independent reasonably regular block differences. No frame-level independence assumption, trimming or post-hoc exclusions. Pointwise bounds; the overall within-budget verdict requires every workload to pass.
selection: Discard pilot from confirmation estimates. Choose the smallest even block count >=24 whose worst pilot CPU standard deviation gives a planned one-sided 95% margin <=1000ns, capped at 120 and the conservative two-hour runtime estimate. Freeze selection before confirmation. Infeasible precision remains explicit; never change the 5000ns budget to fit noise.
boundaries: Complete public Rust dispatch versus prepared native C++ call; caller-side input construction, uploads, submission/fences, readbacks, logs and queries excluded. Existing serial fencing/checkpoints retained symmetrically, with their clock/thermal limitations explicit. GPU command intervals are descriptive, without acceptance margin.
supplemental: Three independent blocks of preparation and prepared-raw Rust diagnostics on all workloads; three allocation processes per workload; eight lifecycle blocks per SDR/HDR context type, eight unused-context warm create/destroy pairs within each process. Supplemental dispatch timing is excluded from the primary estimate.
lifecycle: Loader acquisition/symbol resolution; separate first pre-create provider/render query; first context creation after that query; first dispatch; used-context destruction after fencing; subsequent unused-context creation/destruction. Fresh-process is not cache-cold. Rust test trace lookup suppressed; residual test-only TLS branch and allocator hook remain. No lifecycle speed gate.
stopping: Fixed confirmation count, no early success or optional extension. A wall-clock watchdog stops before starting another child after 7200 seconds; incomplete confirmation cannot pass. Invalid native execution fails evidence acceptance independently of within-budget/exceeds-budget/inconclusive speed outcomes.
exclusions: No FPS/throughput, every-frame latency, native/driver allocation guarantee, universal hardware support, image-quality research or release prerequisite. Existing records remain unchanged.
